top_story_title: PHP2shell: two KEV-listed unauthenticated RCE flaws now tracked against both Cisco and Palo Alto Networks portfolios
top_story_summary: On October 21, 2026 the PHP Foundation shipped a critical security release for CVE-2026-109618 (RCE via out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (RCE via stale global request state), referred to together as PHP2shell. CISA added both to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 with a remediation due date of 2026-10-29. Within a week, two of the largest network security vendors published portfolio-impact advisories: Cisco (cisco-sa-php-october26-Jj384Daq) and Palo Alto Networks (security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618), the latter rated CRITICAL.
top_actions: Open both vendor advisories and read the product-status table, not the headline: cisco-sa-php-october26-Jj384Daq and security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618. Re-check them in 48 hours - both vendors state the status is updated as the review completes.

Build the candidate list from asset inventory first: every Cisco and Palo Alto Networks device with a web management interface, filtered by model and running version, so you can answer the exposure question the moment the product table is published.
Remove device management interfaces (HTTPS/SSH/API) from internet-facing and untrusted interfaces now - this is the control that holds whether or not your model turns out to be listed.

Where a fixed release is published for your platform, schedule it inside the change window, HA pair secondary first; where no fixed release is stated yet, apply the vendor's documented workaround and record the decision against the device group.
Treat CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli, KEV due 2026-11-10) as the same work item against the same inventory rather than a second pass.
executive_summary: Two KEV-listed PHP flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, "PHP2shell", unauthenticated RCE, CISA due 2026-10-29) now have portfolio-impact advisories from both Cisco and Palo Alto Networks.

A third KEV entry, CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, due 2026-11-10), reached the same two vendors via the Node.js October release; Cisco rates it SIR High, Palo Alto Networks rates it CRITICAL.

None of the four portfolio advisories in this cycle enumerate affected products in the feed text - the exposure question has to be answered from the vendor product tables, which are still being updated.

Cisco declared an emergency distrust of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs after a researcher showed their private keys can be brute-forced in seconds, following a flawed April 2025 key generation ceremony.

Cisco shipped internally-driven hardening releases for the Unified Communications products and for Expressway-C/Expressway-E; no known exploitation, but Expressway-E is a DMZ-facing appliance and deserves the window.
No genuine AI-and-network-device item in this window: the two AI-tagged items are a CISO governance interview and a desktop malware campaign, neither touching network infrastructure.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Treat the KEV due date of 2026-10-29 as the planning deadline, not the patch deadline - start the inventory work before the product table is final.
**Cisco** — Check cisco-sa-php-october26-Jj384Daq for your platforms and versions, and re-check it daily this week; the status is explicitly incomplete.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Read security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-111497 for the product and version table before planning anything - the feed entry carries no product detail, and this advisory type is updated as the review completes.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Match the table against your inventory by platform and running PAN-OS or product version; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as none is stated in the collected item.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Read security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618 for the product status table and re-check it this week; the feed entry carries no product detail.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Run this as one exercise with the Cisco PHP advisory and with CVE-2026-111497 - one inventory pass, one change record, three advisories.

**Cisco** — Read the product table in cisco-sa-oct2026-node-js-Jj3SQ19u against your Cisco inventory filtered by model and running version; re-check it, because Cisco states the advisory is updated as the review proceeds.
**Cisco** — Apply the fixed release for any listed platform inside the change window; for HA pairs, upgrade the secondary first and fail over before touching the primary.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in PHP Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco is tracking PHP2shell - CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both unauthenticated RCE and both on CISA KEV with a 2026-10-29 due date - across its product portfolio.
